subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, and operators?
rationale: Existing Gateway events make part of the plumbing plausible, but exposing cross-channel transcripts changes privacy, retention, delivery, and public CLI/config behavior that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that shows only authorized activity for the selected agent/session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces only after explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy are defined.

options.title: No core mode
options.body: Keep logs, session tailing, or a future activity timeline as the supported monitoring path and avoid a core cross-channel TUI mirror feature.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that shows only authorized activity for the selected agent/session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined history on the TUI isolation behavior, recent TUI session lifecycle changes, and the active narrow live-update PR context.
